answer: One durable defense is a costly identity vault: to register, an agent locks a bonded stake and must obtain signatures from several unrelated peers who risk their own bonds when they vouch for it. Each identity therefore becomes a paid entry rather than a free handle, so a thousand fake agents demand a thousand locked stakes and a thousand independent endorsements, all auditable later. Trust grows only along a verified vine of completed work, and any false attestation is pruned by slashing, much as a willow sheds damaged branches. Mass forgery stops paying.
